findings.title: Overly broad exception handling silently swallows all errors, not just validation failures
findings.description: `except Exception: pass` catches everything, including database errors (e.g. connection loss, lock timeouts), programming bugs, and unexpected exceptions from `add_expense`, not just row-validation failures as the PR description claims. Real failures (e.g. a bug that breaks every row, or a DB outage partway through the import) are silently treated the same as a single bad row, with no logging, so operators have no way to detect or diagnose systemic problems from a low `count` return value.

findings.title: No transaction/atomicity for the bulk import
findings.description: Each row is inserted via a separate `add_expense` call with no surrounding transaction. If `add_expense` commits per call, a large import performs one commit per row (poor performance/lock contention for bulk data), and if the process is interrupted partway (e.g. crash, timeout) the import is left half-applied with no rollback and no way to resume or know how far it got.

findings.title: No feedback about which rows were skipped or why
findings.description: The function only returns a count of successfully imported rows. Callers have no way to know which rows failed or why, making it impossible for a user migrating data to fix and re-submit only the bad rows, and making silent data loss (rows silently dropped) likely to go unnoticed.

findings.title: Unbounded row processing enables resource-exhaustion DoS
findings.description: `rows` is iterated with no upper bound on size. A large CSV/JSON upload (accidental or malicious) can cause an extremely long-running, memory- and lock-intensive request with no batching, chunking, or limit, risking denial of service on the shared sqlite database/process.

findings.title: No deduplication/idempotency for retried imports
findings.description: If a client retries an upload (e.g. after a partial failure or network timeout) there is no idempotency key or duplicate check, so previously-imported rows will be re-inserted as new expenses, corrupting the user's expense totals.

findings.title: No tests added for import_expenses
findings.description: The diff introduces a new public function handling untrusted, user-uploaded data with multiple edge cases (missing keys, invalid types, empty list, partial failures, duplicate rows) but adds no unit tests to verify the skip-on-invalid-row behavior, the returned count, or that valid rows are actually persisted correctly.
